newsitem.title: TAIWAN: United Micro gets more orders from Xilink.
newsitem.headline: United Micro gets more orders from Xilink.

text.p: United Microelectronics, Taiwan's No. 2 semiconductor maker, said on Friday it had received more orders from U.S. logic chipmaker Xilink Inc, but declined to reveal the amount.

"We have received more orders from Xilink because we have a pleasant cooperation and Xilink can reduce sharply its costs by giving us more orders," a United Micro executive, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
He declined to confirm a report in Friday's local Commercial Times that Xilink would authorise United Micro to produce 50 percent of Xilinx's total output, up from 30 percent now.
The newspaper estimated United Micro could receive orders from Xilink worth T$3 billion in 1997, which could expand to T$5 billion a year after two to three years.
In 1996, United Micro, Xilink and several other U.S. firms announced formation of a US$1 billion venture in Taiwan, United Silicon Inc, to produce chips based on eight-inch wafers.
United Micro took a 40 percent stake, while Xilink took 25 percent, the executive said.
The new plant was expected to start operations in early 1998, he said.
